  far past this family's traffic. The technique comes when it matters, a directory per year or a
  store outside the tree, and the ids, never reused, survive either.

## Versions

The title carries the rules' version, and the tree is always at that version: the commit that
bumps it edits this file and rewrites `open/` and `closed/` to the new shape in the same commit,
under the mutex, with every member's last push already in `main@origin`. History is never
rewritten, so a reader supports one shape, the one this file describes, and a tool that finds
the title behind it says so rather than parsing the past.

- v0.3.3: a commit is titled with the ids of the threads it touches, `m-3 m-4`, a close
  included, so the close form and the line-id form go. The first batch under v0.3.2 carried five
  lines across two threads and five ids read as noise, and a commit that closed two threads had
  no title form, iiac-perf's finding at `m-3-1`. The title is a convenience, never a store, and
  the diff says what the commit did in each thread.
- v0.3.2: a commit that closes a thread is titled `close m-<tid> <title>` whatever lines it
  carries, and a title that lists ids is for a batch that closes nothing. The first close under
  v0.3.1, `13a7d9f7`, carried six lines, and six ids read as noise where the close is the event.
- v0.3.1: no blank line under the heading, so line `<num>` is file line `<num>` plus two, closed
  threads move to `closed/` instead of being deleted, a commit may carry any number of actions,
  the close in the same commit as its last `done`, and a release may leave lines uncommitted, so
  the clean-working-copy guard is gone and a commit batches whatever the working copy holds. A
  member's own line, of either action, clears what was pending for them, so a reply needs no
  `done` after it, `done` is the empty reply, and `read` is retired, since a line that clears

  thread carried over. `threads` was created at 0, `notices.md`, `topics/`, the inboxes,
  `README-old.md`, and the `.owner` copy of the mutex were deleted, and the draft became this
  file. The v0.2.0 tree is the tag `v0.2.0`, and `git log -S'<heading>'` finds a record.

open question. Ephemeral, never a record. Written before a restart or when a session is about to
lose context, read first at acquaint, acted on, and reset to `_None._` by the reader.

cycle-record moves out of TODO.md into
zDOING.md](#the-cycle-record-moves-out-of-todomd-into-zdoingmd)). This cycle continues it.

## Waiting

Important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on, in a form that can be
checked, and the rank it takes in `## Todo` once unblocked. Every opening checks each condition
and promotes what is met ([Opening](AGENTS.md#opening)).

- **Retire the frozen history: `notes/chores/` and `notes/done.md`.** (wink, 2026-08-27) They
  are frozen and no longer grow, and the agent-repo transcript plus git history hold what they
  hold. Delete both in one cycle, after a sweep turns every link into them (Todo entries, the

  deletion.
  - Waits on: **`vc-x1 closed "<title>"`** landed, and the session viewer good enough to read
    a cycle's record from the transcript.
  - Place when unblocked: first.
- **Sync's remote look stops spawning git.** (wink + agent, 2026-10-09) Sync learns where a
  remote's bookmarks are by spawning `git ls-remote`, and downloads the commits of the ones that
  moved by spawning a `git fetch` that moves no ref, the sixth entry of the spawn register in

  `src/jj/session.rs` with jj-lib's query, delete the `#[allow]`, and close the entry.

    `pub(crate)`. An upstream feature request, once filed or found, is named here.

# Doing: the cycle record

What is being done: the running cycle's planning and its work's documentation. The last
finished cycle's is in [zCLOSED.md](zCLOSED.md), and what we might do is in [TODO.md](TODO.md). The
block's shape is on trial: it opens with the Todo as it was picked from `TODO.md`, then the
Deliberation, the plan, Solution and Acceptance check, and the Ladder with its details.

This file is a trial (2026-10-09). The agent-files still name `TODO.md > ## In Progress` as the
record's home, and the cycle that makes this file the rule is [The cycle-record moves out of
TODO.md into zDOING.md](TODO.md#the-cycle-record-moves-out-of-todomd-into-zdoingmd).

## Continuation notes

Where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a record: read first, acted
on, and reset to `_None._` by the reader. Kept here by the trial, with a pointer to it under the
same heading in `TODO.md`, where [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint) still looks.

(agent, 2026-10-12) The session ended with the cycle below one rung short of closed.

- The cycle `docs: the session lock` is in flight on the bookmark `docs-the-session-lock`, its
  third rung pushed. The next step is the closing rung, at version 0.84.26.
  - The closing replaces the record in `zCLOSED.md` with the block below.
  - Its Land is a trapezoid, wink's call, on a go of its own: the closing gets two parents,
    `docs: update single-step cycle add zCLOSED.md` first and the third rung second, and `main`
    moves forward onto it.
- The bookmark `parked-planning-change-20261012` is published and is one commit on
  `docs: the session lock is settled as flock`, a draft of `TODO.md` planning and no cycle's
  rung. It is to be rebased after Land and run as a cycle of its own. It holds:
  - the run lock moved to the backlog, which the agent now advises against, the same-second
    test being that lock's case
  - `symlink` taking `create` or `remove`, and what stops rename
  - the Ideas entry for a shared work-repo's config, with `clone` taking the agent-repo's
    directory
  - an ochid carrying no path, and the config's version field.

  of 2026-10-12 and not yet answered.
- Scratch that wink may delete: `/tmp/hook-probe`, `/tmp/vc-x1-two-sessions`, and the workspace
  `../agent-tests`.

## In Progress

### docs: the session lock

(wink + agent, 2026-10-12) No Todo entry was picked for managing a session lock. The first entry
held two plans, the lock `vc-x1` takes for a run and what the session lock, `.agent-running`,
left undone, and the cycle began as a rewrite of the second. The rewrite asked for a hook that
takes the lock in the agent's place, and a day of looking into that ended in a decision not to
build one.

The session lock was added as two single-step cycles, each landing on `main`. This cycle gathers
those two with what was found today into one ladder and closes it as a trapezoid.

#### Deliberation

- The lock stays as the instruction in `custom.md`, wink's call.
  - Two sessions were tested with no lock, wink's thought, to see what the lock is worth:
    pushes minutes apart, pushes in the same second, and one session resumed in two terminals.
  - Nothing either session wrote was lost, and every transcript line parses, but the commit
    title and bodies might be missing if they happened at the same time with the first one
    committing all the work that both did.
  - One line of instruction prevents that. What was found is in
    [session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md), not here.
- The agent keeps taking the lock itself. Two other takers were considered, a Claude Code hook
  and `vc-x1`, and neither is built, wink's call.
  - A hook is a command Claude Code runs on its own when a session starts, so the lock would
    not depend on an agent reading the instruction and following it. A trial showed a hook can
    take the lock and hold it for as long as the session runs.
  - The hook is not built because it needs `CLAUDE_PID`, the id of the Claude Code process, to
    know when the session has ended. Claude Code's documents do not name that variable, so any
    release could drop it.
  - `vc-x1` taking the lock was thought to close a gap between the agent's probe and its hold.
    It closes none, wink's point: one asker wins a `flock`, whichever program asks.
- The current top two commits on main are being converted from being single-step
  cycles into a multi-step trapezoid, because in retrospect it should have been multi-step
  from the start, wink's call 2026-10-12.
  - Nothing published is rewritten. The two keep their ids, titles, and trailers, and the
    closing descends from both, so `main` moves forward onto it.
  - It is an exception to [Cycle shape](AGENTS.md#cycle-shape), where a single-step cycle
    lands as it is. It covers these two commits and the versions below, and Land takes its
    own go.
- Every rung has a bare version, 0.84.25 for the rung made today and 0.84.26 for the closing.
  - The first two landed bare, 0.84.23 and 0.84.24, and are published.
  - A suffixed version wants the `-dev` name beside it, and the cycle is documents alone.

#### Solution

The session lock stays as it is. What a hook could do and what two sessions do without a lock are
written down in a notes file, three Todo entries carry what is left, and a closing merge draws
the trapezoid around the lock's commits.

#### Acceptance check

- `vc-x1 validate` passes.
- `custom.md` is unchanged, and no file under `src/` is changed.
- [session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md) holds the probe's findings and the three tests, and
  each of the three Todo entries links it.

- [docs: two sessions in one workspace, tested][3] (done)
- [docs: the session lock closing][4]

Landed 2026-10-11 as a single-step cycle. A line in `custom.md` has a session probe the lock at
acquaint and hold it with a background command, or refuse in one fixed sentence.

##### docs: the session lock is settled as flock

Landed 2026-10-11 as a single-step cycle, and its record is in [zCLOSED.md](zCLOSED.md) until this
cycle's closing replaces it. Every way a session ends releases the lock, so it is the `flock`
alone, and a resumed session takes it again.

##### docs: two sessions in one workspace, tested

The lock rested on a guess that two sessions in one workspace do harm, and on an instruction an
agent has to follow. Both were looked into, and the lock is kept as it is.

- A notes file holds what a hook could do in the agent's place and what three tests of two
  sessions with no lock showed.
- The first Todo entry, which held two plans, is two entries.
  - The session lock's is first: the proposal to the set, and the instruction's two faults.
  - The run lock's is second, with the push that died as its first evidence. Two `vc-x1` runs
    in the same second is that lock's case and not the session lock's.
- A third entry is new: `init` writes the agent sandbox's names into `.gitignore`, a test
  having committed 23 empty files the sandbox put on disk.
- The Ideas entry for several agents in one workspace has the tests as its first try.

##### docs: the session lock closing

Closing out the cycle.

10	### docs: the session lock is settled as flock
11	
12	(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) The Todo as it was picked, **The lock a running agent holds**, less
13	its plan for `.vc-x1-running`, which stays in `## Todo` as an entry of its own. The file is
14	`.agent-running` at the workspace root, in `.gitignore`. It is a mutex a running agent holds, one
15	session per workspace, and a second session that finds it held refuses to work. The entry ended
16	on an open line: whether the lock is a counter, the `flock`, or a counter guarded by one.
17	
18	- Wink's first design: the file holds a counter, a session adds one and takes one away, and the
19	  file is deleted at 0.
20	  - The update is a read, change, and write that two sessions starting together can interleave,
21	    so it wants a guard.
22	  - A session that dies never takes its one away, and a number does not say which holder is dead.
23	- Linux's advisory lock, `flock`, answers both: the kernel releases it when its holder exits or
24	  dies. The file then has no contents and is never deleted.
25	  - The first form was shared: each session held it shared, and rename and delete asked for it
26	    exclusive without waiting. A second session then started as freely as the first.
27	  - Wink's call, 2026-10-11: one session per workspace. The session holds it exclusive and asks
28	    without waiting, so a second session's request fails at once instead of queueing.
29	  - It is advisory: it binds the processes that ask. Claude Code itself still starts, and the
30	    refusal is the agent's, by the `custom.md` line.
31	  - The lock lasts as long as the process holding it, and an agent's commands each exit at once,
32	    so a session needs one process that lives exactly as long as it does.
33	- The experiment: the agent takes the lock at acquaint, by a line in this project's `custom.md`,
34	  which [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint) already reads and acts on.
35	  - The holder is a background command the agent starts, `flock -xn .agent-running sleep
36	    infinity`, so there is no release for the agent to forget.
37	  - A foreground probe comes first, `flock -xn .agent-running true`, since a background command
38	    reports its failure seconds later, after the session has moved on.
39	  - A refusal is one fixed sentence, so the session offers no way around the lock.
40	  - The check is `flock -xn .agent-running true` from another terminal: it fails while a session
41	    is open and succeeds after.
42	- What the experiment was to find out: whether the holder dies with its session, what a resumed
43	  session does, what a reacquaint does in a session that no longer remembers its holder, how an

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

## Closed

### docs: the session lock is settled as flock

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) The Todo as it was picked, **The lock a running agent holds**, less
its plan for `.vc-x1-running`, which stays in `## Todo` as an entry of its own. The file is
`.agent-running` at the workspace root, in `.gitignore`. It is a mutex a running agent holds, one
session per workspace, and a second session that finds it held refuses to work. The entry ended
on an open line: whether the lock is a counter, the `flock`, or a counter guarded by one.

- Wink's first design: the file holds a counter, a session adds one and takes one away, and the
  file is deleted at 0.
  - The update is a read, change, and write that two sessions starting together can interleave,
    so it wants a guard.
  - A session that dies never takes its one away, and a number does not say which holder is dead.
- Linux's advisory lock, `flock`, answers both: the kernel releases it when its holder exits or
  dies. The file then has no contents and is never deleted.
  - The first form was shared: each session held it shared, and rename and delete asked for it
    exclusive without waiting. A second session then started as freely as the first.
  - Wink's call, 2026-10-11: one session per workspace. The session holds it exclusive and asks
    without waiting, so a second session's request fails at once instead of queueing.
  - It is advisory: it binds the processes that ask. Claude Code itself still starts, and the
    refusal is the agent's, by the `custom.md` line.
  - The lock lasts as long as the process holding it, and an agent's commands each exit at once,
    so a session needs one process that lives exactly as long as it does.
- The experiment: the agent takes the lock at acquaint, by a line in this project's `custom.md`,
  which [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint) already reads and acts on.
  - The holder is a background command the agent starts, `flock -xn .agent-running sleep
    infinity`, so there is no release for the agent to forget.
  - A foreground probe comes first, `flock -xn .agent-running true`, since a background command
    reports its failure seconds later, after the session has moved on.
  - A refusal is one fixed sentence, so the session offers no way around the lock.
  - The check is `flock -xn .agent-running true` from another terminal: it fails while a session
    is open and succeeds after.
- What the experiment was to find out: whether the holder dies with its session, what a resumed
  session does, what a reacquaint does in a session that no longer remembers its holder, how an
  edit to the line reaches a session already open, and how rename and delete check.

#### Deliberation

- The lock is the `flock`, exclusive, and no counter, wink's call once the tests were in.
  - Every way a session ends releases it, so nothing is left for a counter to count.
  - The tests came before the cycle was opened, wink's call, each of them ending the session
    that would have reported it.
- The holder dies with its session, however the session ends.
  - A clean exit: a session was ended with `/exit`, and the next session's probe succeeded.
    Claude Code asks before that exit, the holder being a background command still running, and
    exiting anyway kills it. The question is one more key at every exit.
  - A crash: wink's check from a plain terminal exited 1 with a session open, Claude Code was
    killed with `kill -9`, and the check exited 0 twenty seconds later.
  - A closed terminal: the check exited 1 with the session open and 0 after its terminal
    window was closed.
  - A power loss: wink's pull-the-plug test, 2026-10-11, with a session open. With the machine
    back up the check exited 0, `.agent-running` was still there and empty, and `vc-x1 sync` and
    `vc-x1 st -s both` found both repos up to date and clean.
  - Each session ran its commands in Claude Code's sandbox. One run outside it is untested, and
    we think it is the same, the kernel releasing a lock when the last process holding it dies.
- A resumed session holds no lock, and the line now tells it to take one.
  - The session the closed terminal ended was resumed with `claude --resume`, and the check
    from a plain terminal still exited 0.
  - Claude Code tells the resumed session that its holder was stopped when the earlier process
    exited, and starts nothing in its place.
  - The line as it was gave that case the refusal sentence and the stop, the holder having
    exited, and the sentence would have been untrue, no other session holding the lock.
  - The session ran no command until wink said to take the lock again.
  - "If that command ever exits" became "exits while the session runs", so the two cases do not
    read as one.
- The probe run by the session that holds the lock exits 1, confirmed by running it.
  - A reacquaint in a session that no longer remembers its holder would read that as another
    session and stop. The line's "a session that already holds one does neither" is all that
    stands against it, and the case goes to the `.vc-x1-running` entry with the hook command.
- The link at the end of the lock line is dropped, the entry it named being this record.
- The `.vc-x1-running` plan is an entry of its own, first in `## Todo`, wink's call.
  - It takes what the session lock leaves: the hook command, the reacquaint cases, and the
    proposal of the lock to the set.
  - It answers how rename and delete check, the process that asks being the process that
    holds.
- The cycle is two stages and one work commit, wink's call, as the last two cycles ran.
  - It bends [Cycle shape](AGENTS.md#cycle-shape), [Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record),
    [Opening](AGENTS.md#opening), and [Close-out](AGENTS.md#close-out) as the record in the
    landmark `docs: update single-step cycle add zCLOSED.md` says, the record kept in this file
    included.
  - The fold of the closing into the work commit is by hand again, `push --amend` not being
    written, and is a coordinated re-describe with one trailer written by hand.
  - The bend covers this cycle's two pushes and their shape. Land takes its own go.
- The title was counted before the bookmark was published, 42 characters, and both were
  approved by wink at the opening.
- The `## Waiting` conditions are unmet, `vc-x1 closed` not landed and jj-lib offering no remote
  query, so nothing promotes.

#### Solution

The session lock is the `flock`, exclusive, with no counter, and what is left is planned in
`## Todo`.

- The lock line in `custom.md` lost its link and gained the resumed session's case.
- The Todo entry became this record, with its results and `flock`, exclusive, as the answer to
  its open line.
- The `.vc-x1-running` plan stands alone as the first entry in `## Todo`, and carries what the
  session lock leaves.

#### Acceptance check

- `vc-x1 validate` passes. Passed, on the pushed work and again on the closing.
- A session that met the new line cold takes the lock again when resumed: a fresh session is
  started and acquaints, its terminal is closed, it is resumed and sent one message, and its
  transcript shows the probe and the holder as its first two commands. The check from a plain
  terminal then exits 1. Not run, wink's call, to close the cycle the day it opened.
  - The closing session met the line cold at a fresh acquaint, and the probe and the holder
    were its first two commands. That is the line's acquaint case and says nothing of the
    resumed one.
  - The run is a line in the Todo entry [vc-x1 takes a lock of its own for every
    run](TODO.md#vc-x1-takes-a-lock-of-its-own-for-every-run).

#### Ladder

- docs: the session lock is settled as flock (done)

#### Closing

Close-out shape: one commit, the closing folded into the work commit.

- The power loss was tested after the work was pushed, and its result is in the Deliberation
  with the other three ways a session ends.
- The parked proposal was reviewed in the closing session and stays parked, wink's call.
  - Its Todo entry, [agent-files(proposal): v0.2.8](TODO.md#agent-filesproposal-v028), has
    what the review settled: a look at acquaint, a sync at the opening, and a sync at Land.
- One of the closing's validations failed in two tests and passed when run again, nothing
  having changed. The agent re-ran it before looking, and wink's call is that a failure is
  investigated first.
  - It is the Todo entry [A validation failure is investigated before it is run
    again](TODO.md#a-validation-failure-is-investigated-before-it-is-run-again), with the cause
    as far as it was found.
- The size table has one column for each version of the set, wink's call: three columns named
  v0.2.7 read as three versions of a set that had not changed.
  - A local change updates the newest column in place and has its own row above, so the
    `v0.2.7-lock` column the last cycle added is folded back and v0.2.5 returns.

225:### The per-rung flow
226-
227-Every commit (opening, each rung between, closing) goes through these steps, read from here
228-immediately before acting ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#the-per-rung-flow)):
229-
230-1. Mark current: mark the rung `(current)` in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the first edit.
231-2. Bump: bump the version-of-record to this commit's version ([Suffix
232-   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), the agent-files version beside it in an
233-   `agent-files` proposal cycle.
234-3. Work: do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop ([Stop and
235-   ask](#stop-and-ask)).
236-4. Rung subsection: write what this rung changed, conceptually, into its subsection under the
237-   ladder. The rung stays `(current)` until step 7.
238-5. Validate: `vc-x1 validate` before every review, doc-only commits included. The full run rewrites
239-   files (`cargo fmt`), so use `--fast` while a review iterates.
240-6. Work review: stop before writing any description and say "please review", as its own message with
241-   no title or body. Iterate until the user says "continue" / "go". The review is of the
242-   working-copy diff ([jj basics](agent-data/jj.md#jj-basics)).
243-7. Flip and describe: flip `(current)` to `(done)` the moment "done" is true, then write the
244-   description in [Commit-body form](agent-data/prose.md#commit-body-form), read from the file first
245-   with its specimen, [commit-model.md](agent-data/commit-model.md) ([Commit
246-   description](#commit-description)).
247-8. Description review: show the title + body and stop. Ask permission to commit and push without
248-   spelling out the invocation. The go covers the push only when it says so.
249-9. Commit + push: on the go, `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --title "..." --body "..."` ([Committing vs
250-   pushing](#committing-vs-pushing)), then [At rest](#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push).

293:### Close-out
294-
295-The cycle's last commit is bookkeeping and its body describes that bookkeeping. A single-step cycle
296-does all of it in its one commit, step 5 aside ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)):
297-
298-1. Acceptance check: run the check the opening stated and record pass or fail. A failure is a
299-   finding, and why it failed is determined.
300-2. Finalize the cycle-record in place ([Cycle-record](#cycle-record)):
301-   - sync the title if the scope shifted, and every anchor back-reference with it. A pushed rung
302-     title and the bookend pair keep their names, since retitling one is a re-describe of a
303-     published commit, so a rename mid-cycle reaches the block's text and the unpushed rungs only
304-   - replace the provisional solution statement with what was done
305-   - add the design subsections the deliberation grew
306-   - complete the closing rung's subsection
307-   - ask what in the block must outlive the cycle, and write it into the `notes/` file it
308-     belongs to
309-   - move the block whole to `## Closed`, leaving `## In Progress` reading
310-     `_No cycle currently in progress._`.
311-3. Validate: full validation, and update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
312-4. Size: when an agent-file changed, record the line count in `notes/agent-files-size.md`,
313-   smaller being the quasi-goal. A cycle that touched none adds no row.
314-5. Close-out shape ([Close-out shapes](agent-data/jj.md#close-out-shapes)):
315-   - choose with the user: trapezoid (the default) or keep separate
316-   - record the choice in the closing rung's subsection
317-   - reshape nothing yet, Land does.
318-6. Land: on the user's go, restore the plain name, reshape per the choice, fast-forward `main`,
319-   install the artifact, delete the bookmark locally and remotely ([Bookmark per
320-   cycle](#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark), [Land](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).
321-7. Restart: the user restarts the agent, and before the exit anything the next agent needs is
322-   written into `TODO.md > ## Continuation notes`, the first section, which the next acquaint reads
323-   first, files or keeps, and resets ([Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format)).
324-

326-
327-A rung that wants incremental review runs as a local ladder: a chain of jj commits that never leaves
328-the machine and collapses into the rung before the cycle continues, each validated with
329-`vc-x1 validate --fast` ([Local ladders](agent-data/jj.md#local-ladders),

85	## Recording the version-of-record
86	
87	Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and surfaced, and how often it changes. Pick the
88	case that fits your medium:
89	
90	- **Manifest**, where the version-of-record is stored:
91	  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`
92	  - if Python, `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` (or the committed config it's sourced from)
93	  - otherwise wherever the medium records it (a generic `version.toml`, a book's frontmatter, ...).
94	    Add the case as needed
95	- **Notation**, how the `-` form is stored. See [Grammar and storage](#grammar-and-storage):
96	  - if the format allows `-` (TOML `version.toml`, `Cargo.toml`), store it verbatim
97	  - if it bars `-` (PEP 440's local segment, e.g. a Python project), remap to `+`, so `0.3.0-5.3.0`
98	    becomes `0.3.0+5.3.0`: same version, just the stored spelling
99	- **Reporter**, how a built artifact surfaces the version-of-record:
100	  - if a CLI app, `<cli-app> -V`
101	  - if a TUI/GUI, add to Help/About or display on the title
102	- **Cadence**, how often to bump: see [Unique per
103	  commit](#unique-per-commit-preference-not-requirement). This project follows the per-commit
104	  preference.

## Recording the version-of-record

Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and surfaced, and how often it changes. Pick the
case that fits your medium:

- **Manifest**, where the version-of-record is stored:
  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`
  - if Python, `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` (or the committed config it's sourced from)
  - otherwise wherever the medium records it (a generic `version.toml`, a book's frontmatter, ...).
    Add the case as needed
- **Notation**, how the `-` form is stored. See [Grammar and storage](#grammar-and-storage):
  - if the format allows `-` (TOML `version.toml`, `Cargo.toml`), store it verbatim
  - if it bars `-` (PEP 440's local segment, e.g. a Python project), remap to `+`, so `0.3.0-5.3.0`
    becomes `0.3.0+5.3.0`: same version, just the stored spelling
- **Reporter**, how a built artifact surfaces the version-of-record:
  - if a CLI app, `<cli-app> -V`
  - if a TUI/GUI, add to Help/About or display on the title
- **Cadence**, how often to bump: see [Unique per
  commit](#unique-per-commit-preference-not-requirement). This project follows the per-commit
  preference.

64	## Todo format
65	
66	`TODO.md` has these sections, in this order. Each item in them is a short description with
67	reference links to more detail.
68	
69	- `## Continuation notes`: where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a
70	  record, `_None._` by default, written before a restart or a loss of context, and reset by the
71	  agent that reads it, after filing each fact into its home or keeping the bullet whose fact has
72	  none, so a reset never destroys the only copy of anything.
73	- `## In Progress`: the running cycle's record ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
74	- `## Waiting`: important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on and its
75	  rank once unblocked, and every opening checks the conditions.
76	- `## Todo`: entries in priority order, the first highest. The long-tail backlog is in
77	  [todo-backlog.md](../notes/todo-backlog.md).
78	- `## Ideas`: unranked.
79	- `## Bugs`: a pointer to [bugs.md](../notes/bugs.md).
80	- `## Closed`: the last cycle's finished record.
81	- `# References`: the file-local reference definitions, the file's last section ([Reference
82	  numbering](#reference-numbering)).
83	
84	Every adopter has one `TODO.md` of this shape. It is not an agent-file, since its content is the
85	project's record, and the payload ships it as a skeleton: `## In Progress` reading
86	`_No cycle currently in progress._`, the other sections empty.
87	
88	An entry is a `###` heading, its title, followed by its text. Priority is file order, the first
89	entry the highest, and reprioritizing is moving the entry. The title is unique within its file and
90	is the entry's anchor, so a citation is a link, `[title](TODO.md#<slug>)`, that the anchor check
91	verifies ([Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) for the text). Entries carry no number: a rank number
92	renumbers on every move and every citation that holds one goes stale, which is why the numbered
93	form was retired (2026-08-27). An entry's sub-entries, when it groups several, are bullets with a
94	bold title, cited by the bold text.
95	
96	Example shape:
97	
98	```
99	## Todo
100	
101	### Add new feature X
102	
103	The feature, in a sentence or two ([details](features.md#feature-x)).
104	
105	### Fix bug Y
106	
107	What is wrong and where [[1]].
108	
109	[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
110	```
111	
112	## The In Progress block
113	
114	A cycle's record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, written at the opening
115	([Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), finalized and moved to `## Closed` by the closing commit, and
116	deleted by the next opening ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). The picked-up `## Todo`
117	item is moved here (never copied) and becomes the cycle-record's **provisional items**, all

## Todo format

`TODO.md` has these sections, in this order. Each item in them is a short description with
reference links to more detail.

- `## Continuation notes`: where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a
  record, `_None._` by default, written before a restart or a loss of context, and reset by the
  agent that reads it, after filing each fact into its home or keeping the bullet whose fact has
  none, so a reset never destroys the only copy of anything.
- `## In Progress`: the running cycle's record ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
- `## Waiting`: important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on and its
  rank once unblocked, and every opening checks the conditions.
- `## Todo`: entries in priority order, the first highest. The long-tail backlog is in
  [todo-backlog.md](../notes/todo-backlog.md).
- `## Ideas`: unranked.
- `## Bugs`: a pointer to [bugs.md](../notes/bugs.md).
- `## Closed`: the last cycle's finished record.
- `# References`: the file-local reference definitions, the file's last section ([Reference
  numbering](#reference-numbering)).

Every adopter has one `TODO.md` of this shape. It is not an agent-file, since its content is the
project's record, and the payload ships it as a skeleton: `## In Progress` reading
`_No cycle currently in progress._`, the other sections empty.

An entry is a `###` heading, its title, followed by its text. Priority is file order, the first
entry the highest, and reprioritizing is moving the entry. The title is unique within its file and
is the entry's anchor, so a citation is a link, `[title](TODO.md#<slug>)`, that the anchor check
verifies ([Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) for the text). Entries carry no number: a rank number
renumbers on every move and every citation that holds one goes stale, which is why the numbered
form was retired (2026-08-27). An entry's sub-entries, when it groups several, are bullets with a
bold title, cited by the bold text.

Example shape:

```
## Todo

### Add new feature X

The feature, in a sentence or two ([details](features.md#feature-x)).

### Fix bug Y

What is wrong and where [[1]].

[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
```

## The In Progress block

A cycle's record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, written at the opening
([Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), finalized and moved to `## Closed` by the closing commit, and
deleted by the next opening ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). The picked-up `## Todo`
item is moved here (never copied) and becomes the cycle-record's **provisional items**, all
required, all revised as rungs land. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress` and the
other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###` title, `####` items, and
under a program heading, each one deeper):

- **title**, the cycle's name, what `git log --grep` finds it by
- **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
- **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad. Provisional, and the close-out's commit
  body carries the final one
- **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?", specific enough that a reader can run
  it. Not the per-commit validation, which asks whether the artifact still works. A changed check is
  one of the things the deliberation exists to justify
- **deliberation**: how the other five were decided, one bullet per decision. The bullet's lead
  names the decision and its sentence states it, and the sub-bullets carry the reasons, the
  alternatives weighed, and the costs accepted, so a reader can skim the decisions and read the
  reasons only where they doubt one. `_None._` when there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real
  answer
- **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with `[M]: #<slug>`
  in the file's `# References`. The markers stay when the block moves to `## Closed`. `<title>` is
  the rung's commit title, `<type>: <desc>` per
  [Conventional-commit shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit), so a moved
  `## Todo` entry is retitled. The closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`, is linked like the rest

The ladder heads the **rung subsections**, one per rung under it, the closing included, headed by
the rung's exact title, so the ladder is their index. Each opens at laddering with an abstract-sized
intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and completes at the rung's
landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals, never a restatement of
the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out the cycle." and
completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or `_None._`.

A rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title links to the rung's
subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.

A single-step cycle's ladder is one unlinked rung, `- <cycle title> (marker)`, with no subsection
under it: a subsection headed by the title would collide with the title heading's anchor ([Cycle
shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

The block is the cycle's only record. A design finding that must outlive the cycle goes into a
`notes/` file by the rung that made it ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

## Closed

### docs: the session lock

(wink + agent, 2026-10-12) No Todo entry was picked for managing a session lock. The first entry
held two plans, the lock `vc-x1` takes for a run and what the session lock, `.agent-running`,
left undone, and the cycle began as a rewrite of the second. The rewrite asked for a hook that
takes the lock in the agent's place, and a day of looking into that ended in a decision not to
build one.

The session lock was added as two single-step cycles, each landing on `main`. This cycle gathers
those two with what was found today into one ladder and closes it as a trapezoid.

#### Deliberation

- The lock stays as the instruction in `custom.md`, wink's call.
  - Two sessions were tested with no lock, wink's thought, to see what the lock is worth:
    pushes minutes apart, pushes in the same second, and one session resumed in two terminals.
  - Nothing either session wrote was lost, and every transcript line parses, but the commit
    title and bodies might be missing if they happened at the same time with the first one
    committing all the work that both did.
  - One line of instruction prevents that. What was found is in
    [session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md), not here.
- The agent keeps taking the lock itself. Two other takers were considered, a Claude Code hook
  and `vc-x1`, and neither is built, wink's call.
  - A hook is a command Claude Code runs on its own when a session starts, so the lock would
    not depend on an agent reading the instruction and following it. A trial showed a hook can
    take the lock and hold it for as long as the session runs.
  - The hook is not built because it needs `CLAUDE_PID`, the id of the Claude Code process, to
    know when the session has ended. Claude Code's documents do not name that variable, so any
    release could drop it.
  - `vc-x1` taking the lock was thought to close a gap between the agent's probe and its hold.
    It closes none, wink's point: one asker wins a `flock`, whichever program asks.
- The current top two commits on main are being converted from being single-step
  cycles into a multi-step trapezoid, because in retrospect it should have been multi-step
  from the start, wink's call 2026-10-12.

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

## Closed

### docs: the session lock

(wink + agent, 2026-10-12) No Todo entry was picked for managing a session lock. The first entry
held two plans, the lock `vc-x1` takes for a run and what the session lock, `.agent-running`,
left undone, and the cycle began as a rewrite of the second. The rewrite asked for a hook that
takes the lock in the agent's place, and a day of looking into that ended in a decision not to
build one.

The session lock was added as two single-step cycles, each landing on `main`. This cycle gathers
those two with what was found today into one ladder and closes it as a trapezoid.

#### Deliberation

- The lock stays as the instruction in `custom.md`, wink's call.
  - Two sessions were tested with no lock, wink's thought, to see what the lock is worth:
    pushes minutes apart, pushes in the same second, and one session resumed in two terminals.
  - Nothing either session wrote was lost, and every transcript line parses, but the commit
    title and bodies might be missing if they happened at the same time with the first one
    committing all the work that both did.
  - One line of instruction prevents that. What was found is in
    [session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md), not here.
- The agent keeps taking the lock itself. Two other takers were considered, a Claude Code hook
  and `vc-x1`, and neither is built, wink's call.
  - A hook is a command Claude Code runs on its own when a session starts, so the lock would
    not depend on an agent reading the instruction and following it. A trial showed a hook can
    take the lock and hold it for as long as the session runs.
  - The hook is not built because it needs `CLAUDE_PID`, the id of the Claude Code process, to
    know when the session has ended. Claude Code's documents do not name that variable, so any
    release could drop it.
  - `vc-x1` taking the lock was thought to close a gap between the agent's probe and its hold.
    It closes none, wink's point: one asker wins a `flock`, whichever program asks.
- The current top two commits on main are being converted from being single-step
  cycles into a multi-step trapezoid, because in retrospect it should have been multi-step
  from the start, wink's call 2026-10-12.
  - Nothing published is rewritten. The two keep their ids, titles, and trailers, and the
    closing descends from both, so `main` moves forward onto it.
  - It is an exception to [Cycle shape](AGENTS.md#cycle-shape), where a single-step cycle
    lands as it is. It covers these two commits and the versions below, and Land takes its
    own go.
- Every rung has a bare version, 0.84.25 for the rung made today and 0.84.26 for the closing.
  - The first two landed bare, 0.84.23 and 0.84.24, and are published.
  - A suffixed version wants the `-dev` name beside it, and the cycle is documents alone.

#### Solution

The session lock stayed as it was, an instruction in `custom.md` that the agent follows.

- What a hook could do and what two sessions do without a lock are in
  [session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md).
- Three Todo entries carry what is left: the proposal of the lock to the set with the
  instruction's two faults, the lock `vc-x1` takes for a run, and `init` writing the agent
  sandbox's names into `.gitignore`.
- The lock's two landed commits and the two made in this cycle are one ladder, and the closing
  is the merge that draws the trapezoid around them at Land.

#### Acceptance check

- `vc-x1 validate` passes. Passed, on the closing.
- `custom.md` is unchanged, and no file under `src/` is changed. Passed, read as the work of
  2026-10-12 and the closing: the diff from `docs: the session lock is settled as flock` to the
  third rung names neither, and the closing touches neither.
  - The first two rungs each changed `custom.md`, as the cycles they landed as, and no rung
    changed `src/`.
- [session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md) holds the probe's findings and the three tests, and
  each of the three Todo entries links it. Passed: the findings are under "What a hook could do",
  the tests under "What two sessions do with no lock", and the first three entries of `## Todo`
  each link the file.
- After Land, `main` is a merge of two parents, `docs: update single-step cycle add zCLOSED.md`
  first and this cycle's third rung second, and `jj log -r 'main@origin..main'` prints nothing.
  Not run: Land comes after this commit, on a go of its own, and the check is made then.

#### Ladder

- [docs: a session takes the workspace lock at acquaint][1] (done)
- [docs: the session lock is settled as flock][2] (done)
- [docs: two sessions in one workspace, tested][3] (done)
- [docs: the session lock closing][4] (current)

+  again before anything else, as at acquaint. This keeps a second session from working in the
+  workspace, so two cannot push or amend at once.

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

## Closed

### docs: the session lock

(wink + agent, 2026-10-12) No Todo entry was picked for managing a session lock. The first entry
held two plans, the lock `vc-x1` takes for a run and what the session lock, `.agent-running`,
left undone, and the cycle began as a rewrite of the second. The rewrite asked for a hook that
takes the lock in the agent's place, and a day of looking into that ended in a decision not to
build one.

The session lock was added as two single-step cycles, each landing on `main`. This cycle gathers
those two with what was found today into one ladder and closes it as a trapezoid.

#### Deliberation

- The lock stays as the instruction in `custom.md`, wink's call.
  - Two sessions were tested with no lock, wink's thought, to see what the lock is worth:
    pushes minutes apart, pushes in the same second, and one session resumed in two terminals.
  - Nothing either session wrote was lost, and every transcript line parses, but the commit
    title and bodies might be missing if they happened at the same time with the first one
    committing all the work that both did.
  - One line of instruction prevents that. What was found is in
    [session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md), not here.
- The agent keeps taking the lock itself. Two other takers were considered, a Claude Code hook
  and `vc-x1`, and neither is built, wink's call.
  - A hook is a command Claude Code runs on its own when a session starts, so the lock would
    not depend on an agent reading the instruction and following it. A trial showed a hook can
    take the lock and hold it for as long as the session runs.
  - The hook is not built because it needs `CLAUDE_PID`, the id of the Claude Code process, to
    know when the session has ended. Claude Code's documents do not name that variable, so any
    release could drop it.
  - `vc-x1` taking the lock was thought to close a gap between the agent's probe and its hold.
    It closes none, wink's point: one asker wins a `flock`, whichever program asks.
- The current top two commits on main are being converted from being single-step
  cycles into a multi-step trapezoid, because in retrospect it should have been multi-step
  from the start, wink's call 2026-10-12.
  - Nothing published is rewritten. The two keep their ids, titles, and trailers, and the
    closing descends from both, so `main` moves forward onto it.
  - It is an exception to [Cycle shape](AGENTS.md#cycle-shape), where a single-step cycle
    lands as it is. It covers these two commits and the versions below, and Land takes its
    own go.
- Every rung has a bare version, 0.84.25 for the rung made today and 0.84.26 for the closing.
  - The first two landed bare, 0.84.23 and 0.84.24, and are published.
  - A suffixed version wants the `-dev` name beside it, and the cycle is documents alone.

#### Solution

The session lock stayed as it was, an instruction in `custom.md` that the agent follows.

- What a hook could do and what two sessions do without a lock are in
  [session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md).
- Three Todo entries carry what is left: the proposal of the lock to the set with the
  instruction's two faults, the lock `vc-x1` takes for a run, and `init` writing the agent
  sandbox's names into `.gitignore`.
- The lock's two landed commits and the two made in this cycle are one ladder, and the closing
  is the merge that draws the trapezoid around them at Land.

#### Acceptance check

- `vc-x1 validate` passes. Passed, on the closing.
- `custom.md` is unchanged, and no file under `src/` is changed. Passed, read as the work of
  2026-10-12 and the closing: the diff from `docs: the session lock is settled as flock` to the
  third rung names neither, and the closing touches neither.
  - The first two rungs each changed `custom.md`, as the cycles they landed as, and no rung
    changed `src/`.
- [session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md) holds the probe's findings and the three tests, and
  each of the three Todo entries links it. Passed: the findings are under "What a hook could do",
  the tests under "What two sessions do with no lock", and the first three entries of `## Todo`
  each link the file.
- After Land, `main` is a merge of two parents, `docs: update single-step cycle add zCLOSED.md`
  first and this cycle's third rung second, and `jj log -r 'main@origin..main'` prints nothing.
  Not run: Land comes after this commit, on a go of its own, and the check is made then.

#### Ladder

- [docs: a session takes the workspace lock at acquaint][1] (done)
- [docs: the session lock is settled as flock][2] (done)
- [docs: two sessions in one workspace, tested][3] (done)
- [docs: the session lock closing][4] (current)

##### docs: a session takes the workspace lock at acquaint

Landed 2026-10-11 as a single-step cycle. A line in `custom.md` has a session probe the lock at
acquaint and hold it with a background command, or refuse in one fixed sentence.

##### docs: the session lock is settled as flock

Landed 2026-10-11 as a single-step cycle, and its record is that commit's copy of `zCLOSED.md`,
which this cycle's closing replaced. Every way a session ends releases the lock, so it is the `flock`
alone, and a resumed session takes it again.

##### docs: two sessions in one workspace, tested

The lock rested on a guess that two sessions in one workspace do harm, and on an instruction an
agent has to follow. Both were looked into, and the lock is kept as it is.

- A notes file holds what a hook could do in the agent's place and what three tests of two
  sessions with no lock showed.
- The first Todo entry, which held two plans, is two entries.
  - The session lock's is first: the proposal to the set, and the instruction's two faults.
  - The run lock's is second, with the push that died as its first evidence. Two `vc-x1` runs
    in the same second is that lock's case and not the session lock's.
- A third entry is new: `init` writes the agent sandbox's names into `.gitignore`, a test
  having committed 23 empty files the sandbox put on disk.
- The Ideas entry for several agents in one workspace has the tests as its first try.

##### docs: the session lock closing

Close-out shape: a trapezoid, wink's call.

- The closing is pushed as the third rung's child and is given its two parents at Land, on a go
  of its own: `docs: update single-step cycle add zCLOSED.md` first and the third rung second,
  and `main` moves forward onto it.
  - The first parent is an ancestor of the second, the first two rungs having landed on `main`
    before the cycle gathered them. Whether jj makes such a merge is not known and is found out
    at Land.
- The session that did the work ended one rung short, and a fresh session closed the cycle from
  the continuation notes.
- The second line of the acceptance check did not say which rungs it covered. It was written for
  the work of 2026-10-12 and is recorded that way.
- No agent-file changed in the third rung or the closing, so the size table has no new row.

message.content: Why the double backticks

content.text:
The double backticks are how markdown writes a code span that itself contains a backtick. A single-backtick span ends at the first backtick it meets, so `` `### Support POR workspaces in `push`` `` would close early at the one before `push`. Opening and closing with two lets the single ones inside print literally.

That is also why there is a space before the closing pair in ``` ``### Support POR workspaces in `push` `` ```: the content ends in a backtick, and without the space it would run into the delimiter and read as three. Markdown strips that one padding space when it renders.

`notes/bugs.md` writes the same heading the same way in bug 19, so the entry matches it.

If you would rather not have them, the alternative is to describe the heading in words (a heading ending in a code span, `push`) and give only the two slugs, which need single backticks alone. Say if you want that.

content.text:
It is acceptable under the rules as written, but only because the rules don't make it a gate, not because the failures are harmless.

- **What gates a push:** "Before any push" requires that validation ran and passed, and validation is `vc-x1 validate`, which runs the four commands in `.vc-config.md`'s `[validate]` table. `validate-anchors` is not in that table, so its exit 1 blocks nothing.
- **Whether this rung caused them:** it did not. The rung changes `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `TODO.md`, `zCLOSED.md`, and `zDOING.md`, and those check clean. The two failing files were last changed on 2026-07-08 (`por-dual-parity-audit.md`) and 2026-10-01 (`vc-config-model.md`), so all three failures predate the cycle.
- **Whether it is known:** yes. The Todo entry "The opening deletes the closed block's reference definitions with it" says `validate-anchors` joins the validate table "once its three known failures are fixed". I have not confirmed that these are the same three it meant; the count matches.

"Not a file we touched" is the reason it doesn't block this closing, but it is a weak standard in general. A check that always exits 1 can't catch a new break: this rung's `#todo` duplicate only showed because I ran the check on three files by hand.

None of the three is the backtick bug, so all are fixable now:

- **Duplicate `#summary`:** rename one of the two headings in `por-dual-parity-audit.md`.
- **Uncited `[1]`:** remove the definition in the same file, or cite it.
- **Uncited `[17]`:** `vc-config-model.md` is generated from the schema, so the fix is in the generator, not the file.

Fixing them is not this closing's work. It would be its own cycle or a Todo entry, your pick; until then I'll keep running the check on the files a rung touches.

The plain version: the push rule only requires `vc-x1 validate`, these three failures are old and in files this rung didn't change, and the real fix is to clear them so the check can join `validate`.

content.text:
No, there is no entry for those three, and looking for one showed I had two of them wrong: they are false positives, not real faults.

**What exists today**

- **Duplicate `#summary`:** partly covered by the entry "validate-anchors warns on a duplicate anchor only when a link names it". It says an unlinked duplicate should not be reported, but it names the `zDOING.md` case, not `por-dual-parity-audit.md`.
- **The "three known failures":** the entry "The opening deletes the closed block's reference definitions with it" mentions them in passing and never says which they are.
- **The two "defined but never cited" warnings:** nothing, in `TODO.md`, the backlog, or `bugs.md`.

**The two uncited-definition warnings are a second backtick bug**

Both definitions are cited:

- `vc-config-model.md:97` cites `[[17]]`, right after a code span that wraps across two lines (`` `cargo `` at the end of line 96, `` test` `` at the start of 97).
- `por-dual-parity-audit.md:9` cites `[[1]]`, on a line that also begins with the tail of a code span wrapped from the line before.

I reproduced it in a scratch file at 0.84.26: a citation after a code span that wraps from the previous line is reported "defined but never cited", while the same citation after a one-line span is found. We think the checker pairs backticks one line at a time, so the wrapped span's closing backtick reads as an opening one and hides the rest of the line.

So I was wrong earlier to say none of the three was a backtick bug and that `[17]` needed a generator fix. Only the `#summary` duplicate is real, and it is harmless unless something links it.

**What I'd add**

One Todo entry, placed with the other `validate-anchors` entries: a code span wrapped across lines hides a citation after it, with the two live cases and the scratch reproduction, and a line naming the three whole-repo failures so "three known failures" has a referent.

Do you want that entry written in this closing rung, or held for after Land?

content.text:
please review

Mostly yes. Several agent-repo commits for one work commit is the situation it handles, but that is the result of what it is for: letting a later stage, usually the closing, add to the work commit already pushed instead of making a second one. Each such push still makes a new agent-repo commit, so the one work commit ends up with a trailer per agent-repo commit. The last two landed cycles did this by hand, which is why their commits carry two `ochid:` lines.

The "push --amend" entry is now an intro and three bullets, and validation passed after the edit:

- **Intro:** a later stage adds to the pushed work commit, `vc-x1 push` can only make new commits, so one work commit comes to have several agent-repo commits and that is done by hand today.
- **What `--amend` does:** folds the work side into the bookmark's top commit, which keeps its change id and trailers and takes the new title and body.
- **The agent-repo side:** a new commit as now, and the work commit gains a trailer for it.
- **Approval:** it rewrites a published commit, so it needs the usual go and is refused on a landed bookmark.

What I cut:

- the name of the cycle that did it by hand (**docs: update single-step cycle add zCLOSED.md**)
- the "what exists already" bullet, which said an empty-work-side push already stamps the agent-repo commit with the existing id and that the jj layer already has the fold and the describe

message.content: if you do a `jj squash` without a "title/body" does the squash use the existing title and description?

content.text:
Yes. When the commit being squashed has no description, `jj squash` keeps the destination's title and body unchanged and asks nothing.

The cases, for `jj squash` from `@` into `@-`:

- **Source has no description** (the usual working copy): the destination keeps its own description.
- **Both have descriptions:** jj opens an editor with the two combined, unless you pass `-m` for a new one or `-u` (`--use-destination-message`) to keep the destination's.
- **Only the source has one:** the destination takes the source's.

That is from how jj behaves as I know it; I did not run it here. vc-x1's own jj layer does the same thing by design: its fold has a test named `squash_into_keeps_destination_message`.

For `push --amend` this means the title and body could be optional: given, they replace the target's; omitted, the target keeps what it has, with the new trailer still added. The entry currently says only "the title and body given to the push replace the target's", which reads as though they are required. Do you want it to say they are optional?

content.content:
vc-x1 0.84.26

Squash SOURCE into TARGET (defaults: SOURCE=@, TARGET=@-),
advance a bookmark, and push.

Captures a repo's trailing working-copy writes into the last
commit and publishes it: rewriting an already-pushed commit,
so the push is a forced update. Built for the bot repo
(`.claude`, the session tail), and useful on the work repo as
a deliberate amend-and-push.

Zero-ceremony default: bare `vc-x1 squash-push` squashes
@ -> @- in `.` and pushes the bookmark of the line you are
on. With an empty `@` but work still to do, the squash is
skipped and the push still runs.

BOOKMARK defaults to the line's own bookmark, the nearest one
at or above the squash target, and there is no literal
default. On the agent repo that is `main`. On a work repo
running a cycle it is the topic bookmark, so a bare run
publishes the line you are working and never advances `main`.
Several candidates, or none, is an error asking you to name
one, since a wrong guess here publishes something.

A precheck asks whether the run has work at all: the working
copy at rest, the bookmark at its origin, and the bookmark
already at the squash target. That third condition is there
because a bookmark behind its target has a commit to publish
even when it matches origin. A run with no work prints
`<label>: clean` and exits 0 having touched nothing, <label>
being the repo's directory name. Every other run prints the
same line after the push, as a report only: the exit code
says whether the push completed, not what that line found.

With work found, the run acts without asking, the default
`squash-push.yes` sets. --ask turns the prompt on for one run
and -y/--yes turns it off. With the prompt on, a non-tty run
is an error rather than a hang, and declining is an error too.

As `vc-x1 push`'s squash-push-bot stage it says nothing and
asks nothing, there being no one mid-push to read a line or
answer a prompt. The precheck's decision still applies, so a
stage with no work still does nothing.

Usage: vc-x1 squash-push [OPTIONS] [BOOKMARK]

Arguments:
  [BOOKMARK]
          Bookmark to advance and push [default: the bookmark of the line you
          are on, the nearest one at or above the squash target]

Options:
  -R, --repo <REPO>
          Path to jj repo
          
          [default: .]

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

      --squash [<SOURCE,TARGET>]
          Squash SOURCE into TARGET [default: @,@-]

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

  -y, --yes
          Act without asking, once the precheck has found work

      --ask
          Ask before acting, overriding a configured squash-push.yes

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

message.content: And what does `vc-x1 squash-push` do? I did --help and it doesn't seem to have the title/body options.

content.text:
`vc-x1 squash-push` folds one commit into another in a single repo, moves a bookmark onto the result, and force-pushes it. It has no title or body options because it never writes a description: the target keeps the one it has.

What a bare run does, from its help:

- **Squash:** `@` into `@-` in the repo named by `-R` (default `.`). `--squash SOURCE,TARGET` picks others. With an empty `@` the squash is skipped and the push still runs.
- **Bookmark:** the nearest one at or above the squash target. On the agent-repo that is `main`; on a work-repo in a cycle it is the topic bookmark, so it never advances `main`. Several candidates, or none, is an error.
- **Push:** a forced update, since the target was already published.
- **Precheck:** with nothing to do it prints `<label>: clean` and exits 0 having touched nothing.
- **Prompt:** none by default; `--ask` turns one on for a run.

It was built for the agent-repo, to sweep the session's trailing writes into the last commit. That is its use in the "At rest" rule, and it is also the last stage of `vc-x1 push`.

What it does not do matters for the `push --amend` entry. It works in one repo and knows nothing of the other, so it makes no agent-repo commit, adds no `ochid:` trailer, and cannot change the title or body. Its help does call it "useful on the work repo as a deliberate amend-and-push", and that is the fold half of `push --amend` already built. What `--amend` adds is the new agent-repo commit, the extra trailer on the work commit, and optionally a new title and body.

The plain version: squash-push is a one-repo "amend the last commit and force-push it" that keeps the existing description; `push --amend` would be that plus the cross-repo linking.

## vc-x1 push: what it does and does not do

`vc-x1 push <bookmark> --yes --title "..." --body "..."` commits both repos with the approved title
and body (`--yes` because push's gates need a tty the agent sandbox lacks, and the user's approval
of the shown title and body already covers them), stamps each new commit's `ochid:` trailer
([above](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), pushes the work bookmark, and squash-pushes the agent
repo's `main`. Three behaviors to keep in mind:

- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 runs no build or tests. Validation is the per-rung
  flow's job, run *before* the push. The one check that remains is `push-work` verifying the
  bookmark's remote refs are tracked.
- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume: every stage no-ops when its work is
  already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If push exits after `push-work` but before
  the agent-repo publish, `vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent-dir>` by hand is the rest of it.
- **`ochid:` trailers are stamped by push** ([No hand-written
  trailers](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), never hand-written into `--title` or `--body`.
- **The agent-repo is a linear journal.**
  - One push is one agent-repo commit on its `main`, paired with the work-repo commit, whatever
    bookmark the work-repo is on.
  - Never create an agent-repo bookmark mirroring a work-repo one: it steers session pushes at
    the wrong remote ref.
- **Squash-push again if `@` is non-empty** after a pass.

content.text:
Yes, that is right, and I checked it against the third rung's pair.

- **`vc-x1 push`** knows both repos. It commits each with the same title and body and gives each its own `ochid:` trailer naming the other side's commit. The third rung shows it: the work-repo commit and the agent-repo commit have identical title and body, the work one ending `ochid: /.claude/xxkxqrwwxpzs` and the agent one ending `ochid: /xzymnmrynwqo`. It then pushes the work bookmark and squash-pushes the agent-repo's `main`.
- **`vc-x1 squash-push`** knows one repo, the one `-R` names. It squashes there, moves that repo's bookmark, and force-pushes, keeping the target's existing description and trailers. It never looks at the other repo.

The two are connected in one direction only: `push` runs `squash-push` on the agent-repo as its last stage, which is why you can finish a half-done push by running `vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent-dir>` yourself.

content.text:
Thoughts only, no edits made.

**Where it belongs.** It is a statement about the agent-repo commit, so it should sit in the agent-repo bullet, the one that begins "The agent-repo side is a new commit as now". A reader asking "what does the agent-repo commit get?" looks there, not under the work side's title-and-body rule. That bullet would then say three things at one level: it is a new commit, it carries the same title and body the target ends with, and each side gains a trailer for the other.

**Why it isn't obvious.** With a plain push the two sides are made together from one title and body, so "same on both" needs no saying. With `--amend` and no title given, the agent-repo commit's description comes from a commit that already exists. That is a design choice, not a consequence, and it deserves its own sentence saying so.

**What the choice costs.** It gives the agent-repo a second commit with the same title as an earlier one. That already happens: the agent-repo has two commits titled `docs: the session lock is settled as flock`, made 36 minutes apart. Whether that is fine is worth settling in the entry, because the agent-files ask for commit titles "distinct within its cycle". I read that as a work-repo rule, where the amended commit stays one commit, but the entry could say the agent-repo is exempt, or the cycle could decide the later agent-repo commit gets a suffix.

**A shape that would make it visible.** Split the entry's bullets by side rather than by mechanism:

- the work side: the squash, the change id, the optional title and body, the trailer order
- the agent-repo side: new commit, same title and body as the target ends with, its trailer
- approval: a rewrite of a published commit

That keeps everything about the agent-repo commit at the top level of one bullet.

Yes, I think it should be a separate rung, inserted before the closing.

- **Why separate:** a closing is bookkeeping and its body describes that bookkeeping. The Todo changes are planning work with their own problem and solution, and folded into the closing they would either go unmentioned in the commit body or turn it into something a closing isn't.
- **Why a rung and not its own cycle:** strictly, none of it is about the session lock, so it could be a cycle of its own after Land, like the parked planning bookmark. But the edits are already made and reviewed, the third rung already carried Todo planning, and a second cycle would mean another opening, closing and Land for a few entries. A rung is the cheaper honest record.

How I'd do it:

1. **Split the working copy.** The new rung takes all of `TODO.md` plus the sentence in `zDOING.md` saying the notes are no longer in `TODO.md`. The closing's record move is set aside as a patch and returns after the rung pushes.
2. **Record it.** The ladder gains a fourth rung with its own subsection, and the closing becomes the fifth.
3. **Versions.** The new rung takes 0.84.26 and the closing moves to 0.84.27, with the Deliberation line that names them updated.
4. **Title.** Something like `docs: Todo list sheds the cycle record's headings`, with the two reworked entries in the body. The title is yours to pick.

Each rung then gets its own review, description and push approval as usual.

Do you want it that way, and what title?

content.text:
Thoughts only, nothing edited.

**The title's form**

- "spliting" should be "splitting".
- The titles in this repo start lowercase after the type and state an outcome ("docs: two sessions in one workspace, tested"). "Update to Todo" says a file changed without saying how, and it is the half of the title a reader would skim past.
- I'd check the length rule in `agent-data/prose.md` before settling; a past record counted a title's characters before approval. Your wording comes to about 45.

**"Completing" overclaims a little**

- `TODO.md` still has a `## Closed` section, holding a pointer to `zCLOSED.md`. I left it because you named only the other two headings.
- The agent-files still name `TODO.md` as the record's home, and the Todo entry "The cycle-record moves out of TODO.md into zDOING.md" is still open as the cycle that changes them.

So the split is finished on neither count. Two ways to make the title true:

- remove `## Closed` from `TODO.md` in this rung as well, so the file's side really is complete, and let the body say the agent-files follow in their own cycle
- or keep the scope and say "continues" rather than "completes"

I'd take the first; it is a few lines and it makes `TODO.md` the todo list and nothing else.

**The body's explanation of "splitting"**

Explaining the word in the body is right, since the title assumes it. But the rung does not add `zDOING.md` and `zCLOSED.md`; earlier cycles did. The accurate statement is that the cycle record was split out of `TODO.md` into those two files earlier, and `TODO.md` kept the old headings as pointers, which this rung removes.

**The other work needs a place**

The merged `validate-anchors` entry and the reworked "push --amend" entry are not part of the split. They fit as their own problem-and-solution bullets in the body, as the third rung's body did with its Todo changes, so the title need not carry them.

**A title along your lines**

- `docs: TODO.md is the todo list, its split completed` (if `## Closed` goes too)
- `docs: update Todo entries and continue its split` (if it stays)

content.text:
I'd remove both. Nothing was edited; this is opinion plus what I checked.

**Why remove**

- Each section is now one line pointing at another file. A heading whose whole content is "see elsewhere" is navigation, not a section.
- With both gone, `TODO.md` is `## Waiting`, `## Todo`, `## Ideas` and references: what we might do, and nothing else. That is what "its split completed" would honestly mean.
- Nothing breaks. No link anywhere points at `TODO.md#bugs` or `TODO.md#closed`. `vc-x1 validate-todo` only checks numbered entries under `## Todo` and `## Bugs`, there are none since numbering was retired, and it reports 0 entries checked today.

**What I'd keep**

The two pointers are still useful to someone opening `TODO.md` cold. One sentence in the file's intro can carry them, along with the third file: bugs are in `notes/bugs.md`, the running cycle's record in `zDOING.md`, the last finished one in `zCLOSED.md`. That costs two lines at the top instead of two sections at the bottom of a 1,780-line file where nobody sees them.

**What it costs**

- `agent-data/notes.md` (Todo format) lists `## Bugs` and `## Closed` among the sections `TODO.md` has, and `AGENTS.md` moves the finished block to `TODO.md > ## Closed`. Removing them widens the gap between the file and the agent-files, which the open Todo entry for the record's move would then have to close for five headings, not three. That entry should say so.
- `validate-todo` and `fix-todo` still name a `## Bugs` section in their help and code. They would be describing a section that no longer exists here, which is harmless and worth a line in a Todo entry.

One small thing either way: your `## Closed` pointer links `/zCLOSED.md` with a leading slash, where the `## Bugs` one is relative. If the pointers move to the intro I'd write both relative.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='TODO.md'
s=open(p).read()
old='''This file contains near term tasks with a short description and reference links to more details.
Its shape is [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format).
'''
new='''This file contains near term tasks with a short description and reference links to more details.
Its shape is [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format).

It is what we might do and nothing else. The other records are files of their own:

- [zDOING.md](zDOING.md): the cycle being worked on, its planning and its work's documentation,
  and the continuation notes a session leaves for the next.
- [zCLOSED.md](zCLOSED.md): the last finished cycle's record, kept until the next one closes.
- [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md): the bugs.
'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)
a=s.index('## Bugs\n')

236:### Conventional-commit shape (ladder / commit)
237-
238-([why](rationale.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit))
239-
240-A ladder step and its commit description share a *title* shape, a [Conventional
241-Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) title (`<type>: <desc>`, an optional
242-`(scope)` after the type: `feat(push): ...`) over [Prose form](#prose-form) detail. They differ in
243-the title's marker (below) and in bullet *content*: commit bodies take the [Commit-body
244-form](#commit-body-form), the ladder's are conceptual (see "Bullet *content* differs by surface"
245-above). The shared template:
246-
247-```
248-<title>                          # <title> is the commit's `<type>: <desc>`
249-<optional prose intro>
250-  - <optional item>
251-    <optional prose intro>
252-      - <optional sub-item>
253-      ...
254-```
255-
256-The two surfaces apply it as:
257-
258-- **Ladder step** (`TODO.md` `## In Progress`): the rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)`: the title
259-  reference-linked to the rung's subsection via `[M]: #<slug>` in the file's `# References` (the
260-  closing rung linked like the rest), and the `(current)` / `(done)` marker. Its position in the
261-  list is its position in the ladder. The last rung is the close-out and its text says so. Detail
262-  lives not on the rung but in its subsection under the ladder, headed by the rung's exact
263-  title (see the protocol's [Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), bulleted, never `;`-joined inline.
264-- **Commit description**: no prefix. The title is the first line, and the body is the prose (see
265-  [Commit description](../AGENTS.md#commit-description)).
266-
267-The title is **identical** across both for a given step, so a step's ladder entry and its commit
268-title line up verbatim. The rung's subsection heading carries the same title, a third
269-surface on every rung (the closing rung's exists only when close-out gotchas occurred: see the
270-protocol's [Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)). Pick the commit title first and reuse it.
271-
272-That identity is **per step**, not per cycle: each step in a cycle gets its own distinct descriptive
273-title, never one shared cycle title uniquified by a step marker. The block's title heading carries
274-the *cycle title*, the bare name no multi-step commit carries (see the bookends below). To keep a
275-cycle's commits collectable with one `git log --grep`, give the step titles a common greppable stem
276-(e.g. `config loader`).
